mainTopic: Which foods and loaves are valid for an עירוב: broken loaves, missing portions, and other kinds of bread. A new משנה then asks whether money acquires a share in the עירוב.
overview: The גמרא asks why our משנה repeats the rule 'בכל מערבין', which an earlier משנה already taught. רבה says it rejects רבי יהושע's view that only bread works. אביי disproves this from a ברייתא, so רבה בר בר חנה says it rejects רבי יהושע's rule that a broken loaf (פרוסה) is invalid. The reason for that rule is איבה, hard feelings between neighbors, and רב אשי says it applies even when everyone gives broken pieces. The גמרא then sets the limits: a loaf missing only a baker's small חלה portion counts as whole, and so does a loaf joined with a wood chip if the seam cannot be seen. Next come rulings on rice, millet and lentil bread, along with a side discussion of the bread of יחזקאל. Finally a new משנה brings a dispute: רבי אליעזר says paying a coin to a shopkeeper acquires a share in the עירוב, and the חכמים say money alone does not acquire.

steps.title: Why repeat a rule we already learned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that our משנה's rule, 'with everything one may make an עירוב and שיתוף except water and salt,' was already taught in an earlier משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We already learned this once before: 'With anything one may make an עירוב and a שיתוף, except water and salt!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking why our משנה repeats a rule that was already taught in an earlier משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to say the same thing twice for no reason. So the repetition must teach something new. The rest of the סוגיא tries to find out what that new point is.

keyTerms.meaning: We have already learned (in a משנה)
One time, once already
One makes an עירוב (here, joining courtyards)
One makes a שיתוף (merging an alleyway)
Except for

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about the law itself. Nobody disputes the rule. The question is only why the משנה says it a second time.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
We have already learned this one time:
phrases.notes: Refers to the earlier משנה in the third פרק of עירובין.

phrases.english: With everything one may make an eiruv and a merging of alleyways,
except for water and salt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The repetition of 'בכל מערבין' in our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule already appears in an earlier משנה, so repeating it seems to add nothing.

steps.title: רבה: the repetition rejects the view that only bread works
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the משנה repeats 'בכל' to reject רבי יהושע, who holds that only a loaf of bread may be used, and no other food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It comes to exclude the view of רבי יהושע, who said a loaf, yes, but anything else, no. So the משנה teaches us 'with everything.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question. The repetition is needed here because this משנה also brings רבי יהושע's dissenting view, and 'בכל' rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי יהושע limits the עירוב to bread. According to רבה, the תנא repeats 'בכל' right here to make clear that the הלכה is not like him: any food works.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to reject (a certain view)
A loaf of bread
Anything else, another item
It teaches us (the new point)

phrases.english: Rabba said:
It comes to exclude the view of Rabbi Yehoshua,
who said: a loaf, yes,
anything else, no;
so it teaches us: 'with everything.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The repetition has a purpose: it rejects a dissenting opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the repetition, one might follow רבי יהושע and allow only bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בכל' teaches that any food, not just bread, works for an עירוב.

steps.title: אביי: a ברייתא says 'בכל' yet still follows רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא that says 'with everything' but still requires bread for a courtyard עירוב. Requiring bread is רבי יהושע's own view, so 'בכל' cannot be the word that rejects him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: 'With everything one may make a courtyard עירוב, and with everything one may make an alleyway שיתוף. They only required bread for the courtyard.' Who holds bread yes and other foods no? רבי יהושע. And yet the ברייתא says 'with everything'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's answer. He brings a ברייתא that uses the word 'בכל' even while it follows רבי יהושע's bread rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'בכל' and in the same breath says a courtyard needs bread. So the word 'בכל' can sit side by side with רבי יהושע's bread rule. That means 'בכל' does not reject his view on this point, and רבה's explanation fails.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him (from a תנאי source)
Joining of courtyards
Merging of alleyways
Whom have you heard say this? (identifying the author)
And yet it teaches

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say רבי יהושע allows all foods. His point is that a source following רבי יהושע (bread for courtyards) still uses the word 'בכל.' So that word cannot be what rejects him.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection against him:
With everything one may make a joining of courtyards,
and with everything one may make a merging of alleyways,
and they only said to make the eiruv with bread
for a courtyard alone.
Whom have you heard who says:
bread, yes, anything else, no?
Rabbi Yehoshua;
and yet it teaches 'with everything'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that 'בכל' rejects רבי יהושע's bread-only rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא following רבי יהושע's bread rule still uses 'בכל,' so the word does not reject that rule.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה: the repetition allows a broken loaf
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה gives a new answer. 'בכל' rejects a different view of רבי יהושע: that only a whole loaf may be used and a broken loaf may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה בר בר חנה said: It comes to exclude the view of רבי יהושע, who said a whole loaf, yes, a broken piece, no. So the משנה teaches us 'with everything,' meaning even a broken loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבה's answer failed, רבה בר בר חנה offers a new explanation of what 'בכל' adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי יהושע also says a broken loaf cannot be used, even a very large one. 'בכל' rejects this second rule: even a broken piece of bread is valid. This avoids אביי's attack, because that ברייתא only matched רבי יהושע's bread rule, not his whole-loaf rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous answer and starts a new one)
Whole (a complete loaf)
Broken, sliced (a piece of a loaf)

steps.whatToRemember: The repeated 'בכל' in our משנה rejects רבי יהושע's rule that only a whole loaf works. A broken loaf is also valid. The first answer (rejecting the bread-only rule) was set aside because of אביי's ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
It comes to exclude the view of Rabbi Yehoshua,
who said: a whole loaf, yes; a broken loaf, no;
so it teaches us: 'with everything.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבה's answer after אביי's objection, and answers the original question from step 1 in a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation: a different view is being rejected
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בכל' was thought to reject רבי יהושע's bread-only rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בכל' rejects רבי יהושע's whole-loaf rule: even a broken loaf works.

steps.title: Why is a broken loaf not allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יהושע's rule that a broken loaf may not be used for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a broken loaf, what is the reason it may not be used?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now accepts that רבי יהושע forbids a broken loaf, and asks why. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Broken bread is still bread, so it is not obvious why it should be any worse than a whole loaf. The גמרא wants the logic behind רבי יהושע's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A broken piece or slice of bread, not a whole loaf
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And a broken loaf, what is the reason it is not allowed?
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי יהושע's view from Step 4.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 4's new reading of רבי יהושע by asking for the reason behind it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a broken loaf is not allowed for an עירוב according to רבי יהושע.

steps.title: The reason is to avoid bad feelings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן שאול reports in the name of רבי that the reason is איבה, meaning hard feelings between neighbors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן שאול said in the name of רבי: because of hard feelings.
steps.whatsHappening: The question gets its answer. A broken loaf is not allowed because it could cause resentment between the neighbors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not the bread itself. If one person gives a whole loaf and another gives only a piece, the first may complain that the second gave less. So the חכמים required everyone to give a whole loaf.

keyTerms.meaning: Hard feelings or resentment between people
Refers to רבי יהודה הנשיא

steps.whyThisMatters: Because the reason is social and not about the food, the next steps ask when that social concern really applies.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל אָמַר רַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said that Rabbi said:
Because of hard feelings.
phrases.notes: Someone might say: 'I gave a whole loaf and you gave only a slice!'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל אָמַר רַבִּי מִשּׁוּם אֵיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A broken loaf is forbidden to prevent resentment between the participants.

steps.title: What if everyone used broken pieces?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי whether broken loaves are allowed if every participant used one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: If they all made the עירוב with broken pieces, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A follow-up question tests the reason of איבה. If nobody gave a whole loaf, there seems to be nothing to complain about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only reason is resentment, then when everyone gives the same kind of piece, the reason seems to disappear. The question asks whether the rule depends on its reason or stays in force anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them made the עירוב
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
If they all made the eiruv with broken pieces, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי עֵירְבוּ כּוּלָּן בִּפְרוּסוֹת מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the reason given in Step 6 on a case where that reason seems absent.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ban on broken loaves still apply when everyone used broken pieces, so there is no cause for resentment?

steps.title: Still not allowed, because the problem may return
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that it is still forbidden, because the situation could go back to causing resentment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Perhaps the matter will return to its problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי says even this case is forbidden. The חכמים made one fixed rule so that the problem cannot come back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Today everyone gave pieces, but another time one person may give a whole loaf and complain about a neighbor who gave a piece. To keep things simple and safe, the rule of a whole loaf applies every time.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps the matter will go back to its problem

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהושע, a broken loaf is forbidden because of איבה. The rule stays in force even when everyone uses broken pieces, so the problem never comes back.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Perhaps the matter will return to its original problem.
phrases.notes: Next time someone may give a whole loaf and complain about others.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שֶׁמָּא יַחְזוֹר דָּבָר לְקִלְקוּלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is forbidden anyway, because the resentment problem could come back in the future.

steps.title: A loaf missing a small standard amount still counts as whole
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן שאול rules that a loaf missing only the amount of its חלה, or the amount of its דימוע, may still be used for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן שאול said: If the amount of its חלה, or the amount of its דימוע, was taken from it, one may make an עירוב with it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement defines what counts as a broken loaf. A loaf missing only a small, familiar amount is still treated as whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People know that bread sometimes has a piece removed for חלה, or for a mixture of תרומה with ordinary food (דימוע). Seeing such a loaf, nobody will think the owner was cheap, so the concern of איבה does not apply. If more was missing, it would look like a real broken loaf.

keyTerms.meaning: The amount of its חלה, the portion of dough given to a כהן
A mixture of תרומה that fell into ordinary food, from which a portion must be removed
One may make an עירוב for him with it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with the bread itself becoming forbidden. The question is only how the loaf looks to the neighbors: does it look whole, or like a cheap broken piece?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Shaul said:
If there was taken from it the amount of its challah
or the amount of its terumah mixture,
phrases.notes: Think of the 1-in-100 portion that gets taken out because תרומה fell in.

phrases.english: one may make an eiruv for him with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן שָׁאוּל נִיטְּלָה הֵימֶנָּה כְּדֵי חַלָּתָהּ וּכְדֵי דִימּוּעָהּ מְעָרְבִין לוֹ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the broken-loaf discussion: it defines how much may be missing before a loaf counts as פרוסה under the איבה concern of Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A loaf missing only the חלה amount or the דימוע amount still counts as whole for an עירוב.

steps.title: A ברייתא allows only the דימוע amount, not the חלה amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that allows a loaf missing the דימוע amount but forbids one missing the חלה amount, which contradicts רבי יוחנן בן שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: The amount of its דימוע, one may make an עירוב with it. The amount of its חלה, one may not make an עירוב with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן בן שאול with a ברייתא that disagrees with him about the חלה amount. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן שאול treated both amounts the same. The ברייתא splits them: missing the דימוע amount is fine, but missing the חלה amount is not. So the חלה half of his ruling is directly contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)
One may not make an עירוב

phrases.english: But it was taught:
The amount of its terumah mixture: one may make an eiruv for him with it;

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי חַלָּתָהּ — אֵין מְעָרְבִין לוֹ בָּהּ!
phrases.english: the amount of its challah: one may not make an eiruv for him with it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא כְּדֵי דִימּוּעָהּ מְעָרְבִין לוֹ בָּהּ כְּדֵי חַלָּתָהּ אֵין מְעָרְבִין לוֹ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of Step 9 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן בן שאול's ruling that a loaf missing the חלה amount may be used.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly forbids a loaf missing the חלה amount and allows only the דימוע amount, which contradicts treating the two amounts the same.

steps.title: Two Different Sizes of חלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction between רבי יוחנן בן שאול and the ברייתא. One source means the small baker's חלה, and the other means the larger homeowner's חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is talking about a baker's חלה, and that one is talking about a homeowner's חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 10. It shows that the two sources are talking about different amounts of חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן שאול allows a loaf missing the amount of חלה. He means a baker's חלה, which is a small piece, so the loaf still counts as whole. The ברייתא forbids it because it means a homeowner's חלה, which is a bigger piece that really damages the loaf.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This phrase introduces an answer.
The חלה a baker separates. It is a smaller portion.
The חלה a homeowner separates. It is a larger portion.

steps.confusionAlert: The first 'הָא' (this one) is רבי יוחנן בן שאול, who is lenient. That matches the baker's small חלה. The second 'הָא' is the ברייתא, which is strict. That matches the homeowner's larger חלה.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about a baker's challah,
phrases.notes: This refers to רבי יוחנן בן שאול, who permits the loaf.

phrases.english: that one is about a homeowner's challah.
phrases.notes: This refers to the ברייתא, which forbids the loaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two sources are talking about different amounts of חלה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to be talking about the same amount of חלה, so they seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: A loaf missing the small baker's amount still counts as whole. A loaf missing the larger homeowner's amount does not.

steps.title: משנה Source for the Two חלה Amounts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה showing that a homeowner gives 1/24 as חלה, while a baker who sells in the market gives only 1/48.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: The measure of חלה is one twenty-fourth. Someone who makes dough for himself, or dough for his son's wedding feast, gives one twenty-fourth. A baker who makes dough to sell in the market, and also a woman who makes dough to sell in the market, gives one forty-eighth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove the answer it just gave. The משנה shows that a baker's חלה really is smaller than a homeowner's חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A homeowner gives 1/24 of the dough. A seller gives only 1/48, which is half as much. So a loaf missing the baker's amount has lost only a tiny piece and still looks whole.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה.
The required amount of חלה to separate.
Dough.
His son's wedding feast.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why the answer in Step 11 makes sense. The two sources are dealing with two real, fixed amounts of חלה.

phrases.english: As we learned: the measure of challah
is one twenty-fourth.
One who makes dough for himself
or dough for his son's wedding feast,
gives one twenty-fourth.
A baker who makes dough to sell in the market,
and likewise a woman who made dough to sell in the market,
gives one forty-eighth.
phrases.notes: The חכמים were lenient with sellers so they would not lose money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides a משנה that supports the two challah sizes used in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that a baker's חלה is smaller than a homeowner's חלה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת חלה: a homeowner gives 1/24, and a seller gives 1/48.
steps.whatToRemember: A loaf missing only the small baker's חלה amount (1/48) may be used for an עירוב. A loaf missing the homeowner's amount (1/24) may not.

steps.title: A Broken Loaf Joined With a Wood Chip
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a broken loaf that was joined back together with a wood chip may be used for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: If someone joined it back together with a wood chip, we may make an עירוב for him with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a new rule. A broken loaf that has been fixed with a wood chip may be used for an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that broken loaves are not allowed, because they could cause hard feelings (איבה). רב חסדא adds that if the pieces are joined so that the loaf looks whole, it may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: He joined it together (literally, 'sewed' it).
A wood chip or splinter.
We may make an עירוב.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
If he joined it with a wood chip,
we may make an eruv for him with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues defining when a loaf counts as whole for the איבה concern: a broken loaf that has been repaired.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A broken loaf joined with a wood chip may be used for an עירוב.

steps.title: A ברייתא Forbids the Joined Loaf
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא with a ברייתא that says a loaf joined this way may not be used for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: We may not make an עירוב for him with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's rule. It quotes a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא allowed the joined loaf, but the ברייתא forbids it. Since a ברייתא has more authority than an אמורא like רב חסדא, this is a real problem for him.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא. This phrase introduces a challenge.
We may not make an עירוב.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
we may not make an eruv for him with it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's ruling from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that a loaf joined with a wood chip may be used.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא directly forbids the very same case.

steps.title: Visible Seam Versus Hidden Seam
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. If you can see where the loaf was joined, it is forbidden. If you cannot see it, it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is where its seam is noticeable, and that one is where its seam is not noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the case into two situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids the loaf when the join can be seen, because it still looks broken. רב חסדא allows it when the join cannot be seen, because then it looks like a whole loaf and there is no reason for hard feelings.

keyTerms.meaning: Noticeable or recognizable.
Its seam, the place where it was joined.

steps.confusionAlert: Some explain that the first 'הָא' (the visible seam) matches the ברייתא, which forbids the loaf. רב חסדא's permission applies only when the seam cannot be seen.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where its seam is noticeable,
phrases.notes: Forbidden, as in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: that is where its seam is not noticeable.
phrases.notes: Permitted, as רב חסדא said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: a visible seam versus a hidden seam.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every joined loaf seemed to be either always allowed or always forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: A joined loaf may be used only if the join cannot be seen.
steps.whatToRemember: A repaired loaf counts as whole only if it looks whole.

steps.title: שמואל Allows Rice and Millet Bread
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reports in the name of שמואל that an עירוב may be made with rice bread and with millet bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of שמואל: We may make an עירוב with rice bread and with millet bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. Which kinds of bread may be used for an עירוב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an עירוב is made with ordinary wheat or barley bread. This report says that bread made from rice or millet works too.

keyTerms.meaning: Rice bread.
Millet bread.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Shmuel said:
we may make an eruv with rice bread
and with millet bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about what kinds of bread may be used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי זירא's report, both rice bread and millet bread may be used for an עירוב.

steps.title: מר עוקבא Corrects the Report About Millet
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא says he heard directly from שמואל that rice bread may be used but millet bread may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא said: It was explained to me personally by מר שמואל: with rice bread we may make an עירוב, but with millet bread we may not make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: מר עוקבא gives a different version of שמואל's ruling, which he heard from שמואל himself. He limits the permission to rice bread only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא reported that both kinds are allowed. מר עוקבא says that שמואל allowed only rice bread, because millet does not make proper bread.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally.
From the master himself.

steps.whatToRemember: Rice bread may be used for an עירוב. According to מר עוקבא's firsthand report from שמואל, millet bread may not.

phrases.english: Mar Ukva said:
it was explained to me personally
by Mar Shmuel himself:
with rice bread we may make an eruv,
but with millet bread we may not make an eruv.
phrases.notes: It is hard to bake proper bread from millet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא: לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects and narrows רבי זירא's report from Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only rice bread may be used, not millet bread.

steps.title: Lentil bread may be used for an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין reports in the name of רב that an עירוב may be made with lentil bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב: You may make an עירוב with lentil bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list of foods that work for an עירוב. Now it brings רב's ruling that lentil bread works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב must be made from food that people actually eat. So רב is saying that bread made from lentils counts as real human food, even though it is not made from one of the usual grains.

keyTerms.meaning: One may make an עירוב
Bread made from lentils
רב said (a ruling passed on in רב's name)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Avin said that Rav said:
One may make an eruv with lentil bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of rulings about which kinds of bread are valid for an עירוב (rice bread, millet bread, and now lentil bread).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lentil bread counts as food for an עירוב.

steps.title: Even a dog would not eat lentil bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: in שמואל's days, lentil bread was thrown to a dog and the dog refused it, so how can it count as human food?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But there was that bread in the days of Mar שמואל, and he threw it to his dog, and the dog would not eat it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's ruling with a real-life story. If even a dog would not eat this bread, people surely would not either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is about whether the food is edible. An עירוב must be food fit for people. A story showing that even a dog rejected lentil bread suggests it is not food at all, so it should not work for an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (introduces a challenge)
In the days of Mar שמואל
He threw it to his dog

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָהִיא דַּהֲוַאי בִּשְׁנֵי דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: But there was that bread in the days of Mar Shmuel,
and he threw it to his dog, and it would not eat it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא הָהִיא דַּהֲוַאי בִּשְׁנֵי דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב's ruling from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that lentil bread is valid for an עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lentil bread was rejected even by a dog, so it is not human food and should not be valid for an עירוב.

steps.title: That bread was made from a mix of grains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the bread in שמואל's time was not plain lentil bread. It was a mix of many grains, like the bread יחזקאל was told to make.
steps.simpleTranslation: That bread was made of various kinds, as it is written: 'And you, take for yourself wheat and barley and beans and lentils and millet and spelt, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. The bread the dog refused was a strange mix of grains, not bread made only from lentils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer separates the two cases. A mix of six different grains and beans, like יחזקאל's bread, tastes so bad that even a dog may refuse it. Plain lentil bread is edible, so רב's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Other kinds (a mix of different grains)
As it is written (a verse is quoted)
Millet
Spelt

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying lentil bread is bad. The point is the opposite: only a mix of many grains is inedible, while plain lentil bread is fine for an עירוב.

phrases.english: That bread was made of various kinds,
as it is written: 'And you, take for yourself wheat and barley
phrases.notes: Ezekiel 4:9, the bread יחזקאל was commanded to make.

phrases.english: and beans and lentils and millet and spelt, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the story was about different bread.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bread the dog refused was plain lentil bread, which would prove lentil bread is inedible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The refused bread was a mix of many grains, like יחזקאל's. Plain lentil bread is edible and valid for an עירוב.

steps.title: יחזקאל's bread was disgusting because it was baked in excrement
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the bread of יחזקאל was disgusting because it was baked in human excrement, as a later verse says. Its mix of grains was not the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: That bread was roasted in human excrement, as it is written: 'And you shall bake it with dung of human excrement, in their sight.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different explanation of why יחזקאל's bread was repulsive. He says it was because it was baked in human excrement, as the verse states.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step tied the inedible bread to יחזקאל's mix of grains. רב פפא says that what made יחזקאל's bread disgusting was being baked in excrement (Ezekiel 4:12), not its ingredients. Either way, plain lentil bread baked normally is edible, so רב's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Roasted / baked
Human excrement
You shall bake it (as a cake)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
That bread was roasted in human excrement,
phrases.notes: 'That bread' refers to the bread of יחזקאל in the verse.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And it, with dung of human excrement,
you shall bake it, in their sight' (Ezekiel 4:12).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: הָהִיא צְלוּיָה בְּצוֹאַת הָאָדָם הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the challenge of step 19, instead of the first answer in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative distinction: the bread was ruined by how it was baked.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יחזקאל's bread was repulsive because of its mix of grains.
steps.terutzMaskana: יחזקאל's bread was disgusting because it was baked in excrement. Normal lentil bread remains valid.

steps.title: What does 'barley cakes' mean in the verse?
steps.stepSummary: Since the verses about יחזקאל came up, the גמרא asks what the phrase 'and you shall eat it as barley cakes' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'And you shall eat it as barley cakes'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a side question about the verse it just quoted. It is setting up two explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bread was made of many grains, not only barley. So why does the verse call it 'barley cakes'? The גמרא asks what this comparison to barley means.

keyTerms.meaning: What is (the meaning of)?
Barley cake

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'And you shall eat it as barley cakes'?
phrases.notes: Ezekiel 4:12, the start of the same verse quoted by רב פפא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side discussion triggered by the verse quoted in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the verse compares יחזקאל's bread to barley cakes.

steps.title: Eat it in small measures
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that 'שְׂעֹרִים' hints at 'שיעורים', meaning יחזקאל should eat the bread in small, measured amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: In measures.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the first answer. He reads the word for 'barley' as a wordplay on 'measures'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שְׂעֹרִים (barley) sounds like שִׁיעוּרִים (measures). So the verse teaches that יחזקאל ate this bread in small, rationed portions, not as a full meal.

keyTerms.meaning: In measured (small) amounts

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: In measures.
phrases.notes: He's playing on the words: שְׂעֹרִים (barley) sounds like שִׁיעוּרִים (measures).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Barley' hints at 'measures': the bread was eaten in small portions.

steps.title: Prepare it like barley bread, not wheat bread
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the bread should be prepared roughly, the way barley bread is made, not with the care given to wheat bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Its preparation is like the preparation of barley, and not like the preparation of wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a second explanation of 'barley cakes'. He says it describes how the bread was prepared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People put little effort into barley bread, so it comes out coarse. Wheat bread is kneaded with care. The verse means יחזקאל's bread was made in the rough barley style, which fits its role as a sign of hard times.

keyTerms.meaning: Its preparation / kneading
Wheat

steps.whatToRemember: רב rules that lentil bread is fine for an עירוב. The bread the dog refused was a mix of many grains like יחזקאל's, not plain lentil bread. רב פפא adds that יחזקאל's bread was repulsive because it was baked in excrement. On 'barley cakes': רב חסדא says eat it in small measures, and רב פפא says prepare it roughly like barley bread.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Its preparation is like the preparation of barley,
and not like the preparation of wheat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: עֲרִיבָתָהּ כַּעֲרִיבַת שְׂעוֹרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 22, different from רב חסדא's answer in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Barley cakes' means the bread is prepared in the coarse barley style, not the careful wheat style.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר allows paying a shopkeeper to include you in the עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rules that a person may give a coin to a grocer or baker so that the shopkeeper will acquire a share of the עירוב on his behalf.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may give a מעה coin to the grocer or the baker, so that the shopkeeper will acquire a share of the עירוב for him. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. רבי אליעזר says you can pay a local grocer or baker a small coin in advance, and that gives you a share in the עירוב food the shopkeeper supplies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב works only if every resident owns a share of the food. When the neighbors come to the shopkeeper to buy wine or bread for the עירוב, this person is not there, but he already paid. רבי אליעזר holds that the coin is enough to make him a part-owner of that food.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין: 'our משנה.' It marks the start of a new משנה.
A small coin of low value.
A grocer or shopkeeper.
A baker.
That he will acquire it on his behalf, making him an owner.
Food jointly owned by the residents, which lets them carry on שבת in a shared area.

steps.confusionAlert: The person is not just buying bread for himself. He pays so that he will own a share of the food the shopkeeper uses for everyone's עירוב.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of a new משנה.

phrases.english: A person may give a ma'ah coin
phrases.notes: A small coin, paid in advance.

phrases.english: to the grocer or to the baker
phrases.notes: Shopkeepers who live in the same courtyard or alley.

phrases.english: so that he will acquire for him a share in the eiruv,
phrases.notes: When other residents buy the עירוב food, this person is included.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר's opinion, and it is disputed next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a brand-new משנה. It is not connected to the discussion of יחזקאל's bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, giving money to a shopkeeper is enough to acquire a share in the עירוב food.

steps.title: The חכמים rule that money alone does not acquire the עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר: the coin does not make the person an owner, so he has no share in the עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: his money did not acquire anything for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue with רבי אליעזר. They say paying the coin does not give the person ownership of the עירוב food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For movable items, the חכמים require a proper act of acquisition, such as pulling the item toward oneself (משיכה). Handing over money alone does not finish the purchase. Since the person never truly owns a share of the food, he is not included in the עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, meaning the majority opinion.
They did not acquire for him; no ownership was transferred.
His money.
Pulling an item toward oneself, a valid way to acquire movable objects.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds that paying a coin to the shopkeeper acquires a share in the עירוב. The חכמים hold that money alone does not acquire, so the person is not included.
steps.whyThisMatters: The argument depends on a basic rule of קנין: does money by itself acquire movable items? This decides whether paying in advance works for an עירוב.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
phrases.notes: The opposing view.

phrases.english: His money did not acquire for him.
phrases.notes: Money alone is not a valid act of acquisition here.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים לֹא זָכוּ לוֹ מְעוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רבי אליעזר's ruling within the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, money alone does not transfer ownership of the עירוב food, so the person is not included.
